internship.heading: Professional Internship
internship.subheading: A 13-week R&D journey through SentinelOne Hyperautomation, MISP threat intelligence integration, and a final pivot to a production Python microservice pipeline — delivering sub-30-second SOC triage automation at VanRoey (Dynamate).
internship.title: Automating SOC Incident Triage — VanRoey (Dynamate)
internship.context: VanRoey (Dynamate) is a Belgian ICT-services provider running a Security Operations Center (SOC) delivering Managed Detection & Response (MDR). SentinelOne Singularity is the core EDR/XDR and identity posture platform — integrated with Microsoft environments, Fortinet firewalls, and OT security systems. Despite these capabilities, analysts were still manually enriching every alert by pivoting between VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, and internal databases, creating a critical MTTR bottleneck.
internship.objectives: Automate incident triage by developing ≥3 functional SOAR playbooks, integrate independent Threat Intelligence feeds (MISP / CCB / CIRCL) to eliminate vendor lock-in, reduce MTTR to under 30 seconds per alert, and ensure the architecture scales with VanRoey's growing client base without linear headcount growth.
internship.businessCase: Every second of manual triage increases exposure in ransomware incidents. Vendor-only TI creates blind spots when the EDR vendor misses a threat actor. Replacing third-party SOAR licensing (Rewst) with a custom open-source Python stack eliminated recurring costs. Automation decouples alert volume growth from analyst headcount growth.
internship.methodology: Agile-inspired 13-week sprint structure with 2–3 week iterations and a living backlog. A 'Fail Fast' approach tackled the hardest integration first (S1 Marketplace + MISP in Sprint 2), which surfaced a critical STIX 2.1 parser bug and forced an early architectural pivot — enabling course correction without losing the core objective.
internship.synopsis:
During my internship at VanRoey (Dynamate), I was tasked with eliminating the slow Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) caused by manual SOC triage. Analysts were manually pivoting between SentinelOne, VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB and internal databases for every incoming alert.

Phase 1 — TI Platform Selection: I evaluated OpenCTI vs MISP by running both via Docker. OpenCTI suffered from excessive resource consumption and swap memory exhaustion on the server. MISP won on API-driven automation performance and stability. I integrated MISP with CCB and CIRCL feeds via PGP/GPG encryption.

Phase 2 — SentinelOne Hyperautomation: The native S1 Marketplace MISP app failed with persistent HTTP 40000100 and 502 Bad Gateway errors. A deep-dive revealed two root causes: HTTPS was required (fixed via HAProxy reverse proxy + Let's Encrypt), and a confirmed STIX 2.1 parser defect in the Marketplace app. SentinelOne R&D acknowledged the bug with no patch timeline. I pivoted to building custom HTTP API calls directly in Hyperautomation, using GraphQL (85% payload reduction vs REST), pagination for bulk IOC handling, JQ for JSON transformation, and OCSF normalization. Four baseline workflows were delivered: auto alert enrichment, compromised credential detection, agent health monitoring, and MS Teams notifications.

Phase 3 — Rewst Evaluation: Rewst (low-code IT automation) was explored for ticketing workflows. Datto Autotask API blockers, opaque Jinja template debugging, and lack of version control ruled it out for SOC use.

Phase 4 — Python Microservices: With low-code platforms exhausted, I architected a production Python pipeline: FastAPI for webhook ingestion, RabbitMQ for async message brokering, Redis for deduplication and state management, all containerized in Docker. Four workers were built: an enrichment worker (MISP hash/IP lookups), a credential audit script, an agent attention monitor, and a ticketing engine that auto-generates Datto Autotask tickets with enriched context.

UAT was conducted using EICAR test files and simulated PowerShell executions on Hyper-V client VMs alongside SOC analysts Matthias, Joey, and Milan. The final result: a fully tested, documented pipeline reducing MTTR from minutes to under 30 seconds.

timeline.step4Desc: Autotask API blockers, opaque Jinja debugging, and no version control made low-code unsuitable for SOC-grade automation.
